Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the draft renewal materials — we reviewed them with the product and procurement teams this morning. Before we lock in a new agreement we have a couple of structural asks:

- We prefer a multi-year arrangement (2 years preferred) but with a phased capacity ramp tied to quarterly true-ups.
- OptiVenta would like co-terming across three business units so our billing aligns to the fiscal year end (Sep 30).
- Procurement flagged auto-renew: they only accept auto-renew if there is a clear opt-in clause and 60-day window to opt-out; otherwise they require explicit renewal each term.

Can your team propose a safe structure that lets us secure predictable capacity while leaving room for growth/true-ups? Also, pricing sensitivity: we need to understand how year-over-year discounts vs staged ramp credits would look.

Happy to schedule a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful context. High level we can do a 24-month commitment with a staged ramp and explicit true-up windows. Proposed sketch:

- Term: 24 months, co-term to OptiVenta fiscal year (target Sep 30 alignment in year 1).
- Ramp schedule (example): Q1 commit = 50% of year-averaged capacity, Q2 true-up to 75%, Q3 true-up to 90%, Q4 settle to 100% (annualized). True-ups would be quarterly with a 30-day reporting window.
- Pricing: blended unit price that steps down modestly at the 12-month mark if utilization targets are met; early upsell credits for any top-ups in the first 9 months to incentivize go-live scale.
- Auto-renew: we can flip to an opt-in model in the agreement (auto-renew only if both parties execute an opt-in addendum 60–30 days before renewal). If procurement requires manual renewal, we can include a renewal notice schedule and a fail-safe that prevents auto-billing without explicit acceptance.

I attached a quick worksheet that maps example token buckets to discount tiers (CO_TERM_WORKSHEET.xlsx). If that looks reasonable we can translate into a DocuSign-ready amendment and a billing cadence option (monthly vs quarterly invoice).

Would you prefer monthly invoicing for tighter visibility or quarterly invoicing for simpler AP processing? We can support both with an invoice proration policy for the ramp quarters.

If that aligns, I’ll circulate a crisp proposal and pricing table. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best,
Priyom Das

Attachments: CO_TERM_WORKSHEET.xlsx (xlsx), Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_OptiVenta_Q3.pdf (pdf)

Priyom / Karthik — quick internal note after reading Hannah's ask. Key recommendations from pricing/legal POV:

- Offer structure: 24-month agreement with quarterly true-ups, co-term alignment to Sep 30 at the end of Q3. Year 1 effective commit should be conservative to reduce sticker shock; Year 2 should contain an uplift band and enrollment for a tiered discount if utilization > 85% on average.
- Discounting: propose 8% effective discount in year 1 (applied to baseline commit), step to 12% in year 2 provided utilization triggers. Keep absolute floor pricing for overage tokens to protect unit economics.
- Credits & onboarding: front-load $25k onboarding credit that vests against Q1 usage to incentivize adoption. This can be amortized across invoices.
- Auto-renew mechanics: legal will not accept open auto-renew in enterprise procurement. We should provide an "auto-renew opt-in" path plus a manual renewal path. If procurement requires opt-out windows, we can accept a 60-day opt-in confirmation procedure to satisfy them.
- Billing cadence: OptiVenta likely prefers quarterly (procurement-friendly). Recommend default to quarterly invoicing with optional monthly reporting. Quarterly invoicing reduces AP friction for them and reduces Redwood invoice ops overhead.

Risks: aligning to Sep 30 co-term means we may need a proration for the initial partial period if the signature date is not synchronized. Also watch for SLA credit caps — avoid open-ended escalators.

Next steps: I drafted a tidy proposal PDF and the worksheet — Priyom, if you agree, send Hana(n) revised proposal with both billing cadence options and the opt-in auto-renew mechanics. Karthik, can you run the numbers quickly on the blended price impact if they hit 90% utilization in Y2?

Marissa
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom and Marissa — this is much clearer and aligns with our procurement team. A few quick confirmations before we proceed to signature:

- We prefer quarterly invoicing (reduces AP lift). Please show quarterly as the default, with a note that Redwood will provide monthly usage reports for visibility.
- For auto-renew, OptiVenta will accept an opt-in mechanism: Redwood to provide a renewal addendum window 60–30 days before renewal; if OptiVenta signs the addendum it will auto-renew. Otherwise the agreement will expire and a manual renewal will be required.
- Please include the $25k onboarding credit and a 30-day true-up reporting window (we can be flexible on exact dates but prefer the cadence).

If you can update the proposal and re-send a DocuSign link with the co-term proration language (one-time proration in the initial partial period), we can route internally and aim to sign within 10 business days.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Platform Operations | OptiVenta
